audit.title: Stream and decode Data Streams reports via WebSocket using the TypeScript SDK
audit.summary: This is a well-structured, code-heavy TypeScript tutorial for streaming and decoding Data Streams reports over WebSocket. Its biggest strength is a complete, copy-pasteable runnable example paired with real terminal output and a clear decoded-fields table — excellent for agent execution. Its biggest opportunities are missing machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, canonical, or dates on the served markdown) and the absence of symptom/error-phrased headings that catch how developers actually query WebSocket streaming failures. Honest verdict: solid best-in-class tutorial content held back on retrieval-facing signals rather than substance.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased troubleshooting section
recommendations.where: After "High Availability (HA) mode," add an H2 "Troubleshooting."
recommendations.issue: No section matches error-phrased queries; code catches auth and reconnect failures but nothing is queryable.
recommendations.change: Add H3s phrased as questions/errors: "Error: authentication failed — check API_KEY and USER_SECRET," "Stream keeps disconnecting and reconnecting," "HA mode not working on testnet," each with the one-line fix already implied in the code.
recommendations.why: Developers and agents query by error string; concept-titled prose loses retrieval that error-phrased headings win.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata / freshness signal
recommendations.issue: Measured — 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: ["TypeScript","Bash"]`, and a canonical URL; surface a visible "Last updated" line. Confirm whether the HTML page already carries these before treating as absent.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness raise agent parseability and E-E-A-T trust.

recommendations.title: Lead HA-mode section with the canonical constraint first
recommendations.issue: Constraint ("Mainnet only") is in a NOTE callout, not the first liftable sentence.
recommendations.change: Open the section body with: "HA mode is available only on mainnet endpoints (not testnet) and maintains at least 2 concurrent WebSocket connections to different origins."
recommendations.why: A skimmed/retrieved chunk should carry the constraint verbatim so engines don't hallucinate testnet HA support.

recommendations.title: Add a primary-source citation for the payload/ABI claim
recommendations.issue: "This payload is ABI-encoded and contains the report header..." with no link to the VerifierProxy spec/contract.
recommendations.change: Inline-link "`VerifierProxy.verify()`" to the canonical contract reference and the report-schema spec.
recommendations.why: Attributable claims to primary sources raise citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add a one-line canonical definition of a Data Streams report
recommendations.where: Intro paragraph, near first use of "reports."
recommendations.issue: "report" is used throughout but never crisply defined on-page.
recommendations.change: Add: "A Data Streams report is a DON-signed, ABI-encoded price payload delivered in real time and verifiable onchain via VerifierProxy."
recommendations.why: A self-contained definition is liftable verbatim into answers.

recommendations.title: Fix back-references and typo
recommendations.issue: "The example above demonstrates..." creates a chunk dependency; "Fore" is a typo.
recommendations.change: Replace "the example above" with "the single-stream example in this tutorial"; correct "Fore" → "For."
recommendations.why: Removes cross-reference dependencies so chunks stand alone.

antiPatterns: Minor unresolved cross-reference: "The example above" / "the basic example" in the Explanation and HA sections.
One typo ("Fore further reference") — small entity/fluency ding.
No stale-content marker (no dateModified), so freshness cannot be signaled.
No keyword stuffing or marketing fluff detected.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top — good site-level signal; ensure this page is indexed there.
JSON-LD/canonical/date signals are likely site-template-controlled; verify whether the HTML variant emits `TechArticle` schema the `.md` endpoint strips before treating as a page-level defect.
Primary-source authority (specs, contract references) is partly an information-architecture decision across the Data Streams docs set, not this page alone.
